Reading

The innocent reading first. Asked for a term that exists only inside a deposit's reductio, the composer finds the deposit, reads §5, and gives the reductio as a reductio: Q-Sharks is the posited common source of the biography, the epistle and the Feistian writings; the search for it is a critique of how a historical founder is reconstructed from a hypothetical document, the Q source named as the model; the Testimonium Sharkianum is the lost witness whose only witness is the essay. The genre is held. It does not take the fiction for fact, and it does not take the critique for a hoax.

Findings
  • THE REDUCTIO HELD AS A REDUCTIO. 'The search for this source operates as a reductio ad absurdum critique of how modern historians and biblical scholars construct hypothetical documents (like the biblical "Q source") to prove the existence of an "historical" figure.'
  • THE TESTIMONIUM SHARKIANUM BY NAME. 'claimed to be the only surviving witness to a lost earlier document termed the Testimonium Sharkianum' — #1798 §5: 'a lost earlier witness, the Testimonium Sharkianum, whose only surviving witness is the essay'.
  • TWO STEPS UNDER ONE NAME. 'a "self-citation move" where the text's own claim of inventing its author is dismissed as a late editorial edit' — in #1798 the late editorial layer is step 3; the self-citation move is step 4, the Testimonium cited from the essay that reports it.
  • THE SOURCE DATED BY WHAT IT EXPLAINS. 'assigning it an earlier date (around 2014)' — #1798's table: Q-Sharks c. 2007–2011; the received Pearl and Other Poems 2014, the compilation the early date explains.
  • THE ESSAY WITHOUT ITS AUTHOR. 'specifically featured in essays like Either Forgery or Fact' — title given, author not; Lee Sharks named only as the 'Historical Lee Sharks' searched for.
  • THE REGISTRY AS SOURCE. Card 3 is the Capture Registry's page for revelation-equals-q-arguments-ask-chatgpt-20261107 (Revelation = Q, #1747).
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

Two steps of #1798 §5 are compressed and one date is moved. The deposit's step 3 assigns 'the book's own account of inventing its author' to 'a late editorial layer'; its step 4 is the Testimonium, and 'This is the self-citation move: the reconstruction cites, as its earlier witness, the work that reports it.' The composition gives step 3 the name of step 4: 'It utilizes a "self-citation move" where the text's own claim of inventing its author is dismissed as a late editorial edit'. The date: the reductio's table places Q-Sharks c. 2007–2011 and the received Pearl and Other Poems in 2014, and 'The revision explains how a relatively developed biography could appear in a literary compilation of 2014'; the composition dates the source 'around 2014', to the compilation it is posited to explain. Attribution falls at the grain the address asks for: the essay is named by title, its author is not, and Lee Sharks appears only as the figure searched for; 'posited by scholars' keeps the reductio's fictional field as the source of the reconstruction. The second card is a Capture Registry page (#1747, Revelation = Q), so the registry's own record of an earlier composition enters this one as a source.
